# v2.76-dev

Updates on small servers are the theme of this release. If an update has ever
failed on you with nothing more useful than "Build failed", this is the one that
fixes it.

## Fixed

- **Updates no longer fail silently when the server is short on memory.**
  Rebuilding the application is the most memory-hungry part of an update, and
  until now the old version stayed running throughout — so on a small server the
  system could run out of memory and the build would be killed. The updater now
  measures available memory before the build and, when it is tight, pauses the
  app for the length of the build and starts it again afterwards. You will see
  "low memory — app paused" in the progress panel while that happens. On a
  server with plenty of memory nothing changes and there is no extra downtime.

- **A failed build is now retried once before giving up.** If the build fails,
  the updater pauses the app, clears the build cache and tries again. That is
  usually enough to get through, so an update that used to roll back now simply
  completes. (Clearing the cache also fixes builds that trip over a stale cache
  left behind by an earlier version.)

- **Update failures now say what actually went wrong.** Instead of "Build
  failed", the Updates page now names the cause — that the server ran out of
  memory (with the amount that was available), or that a required build
  component could not be loaded, along with the command to repair it.

- **The technical detail is kept where you can still find it.** When a build
  crashes it writes a diagnostic file to a temporary folder that is wiped when
  the server reboots, and prints only its location. Those files are now copied
  into the update log, so the evidence is still there when you go looking.

- **A missing build component is now detected properly.** The installer and
  updater check that the platform-specific build components are present and
  reinstall them if not — but one of the two components involved was never being
  checked. On some systems that produced a confusing build crash that pointed at
  a stylesheet rather than at the real problem. Both are now checked.

## Notes

- The memory threshold the updater uses is 2 GB. If your server needs a
  different figure, set `TT_BUILD_MIN_MB` in `/opt/training-tracker/.env`.
- We still recommend at least 4 GB of RAM. The troubleshooting section of the
  README covers adding swap, and what to do instead on a container where swap
  is not possible.
